name: Trieng
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Từ ngữ âm hay còn gọi là từ âm vị học (phonological word) trong tiếng Bh'noong được xác định như một hoặc hai âm tiết, được phân định bằng cách ngắt khi phát âm. Ở hình thức hai âm tiết, từ ngữ âm bao gồm một âm tiết chính và một âm tiết phụ. Âm tiết chính bao giờ cũng mang trọng âm và đứng sau âm tiết phụ. Khi phát âm, âm tiết phụ được phát âm nhẹ và lướt nhằm thể hiện rõ trọng âm của từ ở âm tiết chính. [I.2:] Trong đó, cv là âm tiết phụ; âm tiết phụ không có âm cuối; C1V±C2 là âm tiết chính, mang trọng âm
new_statements.translation: The phonetic word, also called the phonological word, in Bh'noong is defined as one or two syllables, delimited by a break in pronunciation. In the two-syllable form, the phonetic word consists of a main syllable and a minor syllable. The main syllable always bears the stress and stands after the minor syllable. In pronunciation the minor syllable is pronounced lightly and glided over, so as to bring out clearly the word's stress on the main syllable. [I.2:] Here cv is the minor syllable; the minor syllable has no coda; C1V±C2 is the main syllable, bearing the stress.
new_statements.citation: Nguyễn Đăng Châu. 2008. Cơ cấu ngữ âm tiếng Bh'noong (trong ngôn ngữ Giẻ-Triêng). Báo cáo tổng kết đề tài cấp Bộ MS B2007-ĐN03-23. Đà Nẵng: Đại học Đà Nẵng. Chương I, mục I.1 'Từ ngữ âm học tiếng Bh'noong' and I.2 'Mô hình cấu trúc từ ngữ âm tiếng Bh'noong'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bh'noong words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (minor syllable + main syllable). In a two-syllable phonological word the stress always falls on the main syllable, which is the second/final syllable; the preceding minor (pre-)syllable is unstressed, short and weak. Effectively fixed word-final (main-syllable) stress, the general Bahnaric/Mon-Khmer sesquisyllabic pattern.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. Monosyllables cannot show stress contrastively ('âm tiết trong từ đơn tiết không có điều kiện thể hiện trọng âm một cách rõ rệt như âm tiết chính'). Bùi Đăng Bình 2020 mentions 3- and 4-syllable Bhnong words but gives no stress rule for them.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word ('từ ngữ âm'), delimited by pause; words are monosyllabic (1324 of 1536 basic words, 86.19%) or sesquisyllabic (212, 13.81%: minor syllable cv + main syllable C1V(C2)). The author checked waveform, intensity, pitch and duration of sample words: the minor syllable's peak is lower than the main syllable's. No phrase-level or citation-form discussion. Language stated to be toneless ('ngôn ngữ chưa hình thành thanh điệu').
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Bh'noong (Bhnong, Bnoong) of Phước Sơn district, Quảng Nam -- the largest local group of the official Giẻ-Triêng ethnic group -- which the author treats as a dialect of the 'Giẻ-Triêng language'. Bh'noong has no ISO 639-3 or Glottolog code ('Bnoong' matches no languoid) and its assignment to Trieng [stg]/trie1243 rather than Jeh [jeh]/jehh1245 is not established by any source seen: Ethnologue's stg is 'the language of the Gie Trieng ethnic group' (alt names incl. Dgiéh, Tareh, Ta-Rieng, Talieng), but Glottolog places trie1243 under West Bahnaric > Triengic (trie1245) with Talieng (tali1257), i.e. the Tariang-type lect of Nam Giang (Quảng Nam) and Dak Cheung (Laos), whereas Vietnamese authors class Giẻ-Triêng incl. Bh'noong as North Bahnaric. No description of Trieng proper (Nam Giang/Đăk Glei) was found. Nguyễn Hữu Hoành 2004 (wishlist) would settle the affiliation; if the catalog wants only code-bearing lects, this should be filed as Bh'noong (no code, Giẻ-Triêng umbrella) rather than merged into trie1243.

sources.locator: Chapter I, sec. I.1 (report pp.13-14 per the table of contents) and sec. I.2 (p.15); the web reproduction carries no page numbers
sources.note: Sec. I.1 (report pp.13-14 per TOC): the phonological word is one or two syllables; in the two-syllable form the main syllable always bears the stress and follows the minor syllable, which is pronounced lightly; sec. I.2 (p.15): model cv.C1V(C2), main syllable stressed. No tones. Describes Bh'noong (Phước Sơn, Quảng Nam), a Giẻ-Triêng local group, not Trieng of Nam Giang/Đăk Glei by name.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul & Pascale Jacq. 2003. A Handbook of Comparative Bahnaric, vol. 1: West Bahnaric. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics (PL-551).
sources.note: Sec. 4.2 pp.33-34, family level: 'Most WB languages are sesquisyllabic... In the latter case a stressed mainsyllable is preceded by a minorsyllable... Sesquisyllabism is typical for Bahnaric'. Not Trieng-specific.

No descriptive references: only Sidwell 2009 (overview, p.83 subclassification comment) and Schliesinger 1998 (ethnographic). Classification Austroasiatic > Bahnaric > West Bahnaric > Triengic (after Sidwell 2021: 185-186); coordinates 15.50N 107.515E (Nam Giang, Quảng Nam). Alt names Dgiéh, Giang Ray, Gie-Trieng, Pin, Strieng, Ta-Rieng, Talieng, Tareh, Treng; 'Bnoong' matches no languoid.

sources.citation: Person, Stephanie Lynn. 2022. Li Xei: A phonology of an understudied Bahnaric language in central Vietnam. MA thesis, University of North Dakota.
sources.note: Grep of the text: no stress statement; Li Xei is sesquisyllabic, North Bahnaric close to Jeh; speakers officially Giẻ Triêng and 'called Trieng by outsiders' but autonym Li Xei. Not Trieng [stg].
